doc.title: Architecture Plan
doc.snippet: Defines service architecture with Backend API (FastAPI), MCP Server (Python MCP SDK), Telegram Bot (python-telegram-bot), and Redis. Services communicate via Docker network with isolated annie-network.

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.section: Docker Compose Service Definitions, Services and Modules
doc.snippet: Defines Docker Compose structure with all services (backend, mcp-server, telegram-bot, redis), network configuration (annie-network bridge), volumes (redis-data, development volumes), and health checks. Service dependencies: backend depends on redis and mcp-server; telegram-bot depends on backend.

doc.snippet: Story 1.2 establishes containerized development environment with Docker Compose configuration, Dockerfiles for all services, health checks, and volume mounts. Maps to Tasks 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5.

constraint.description: Backend service must wait for Redis and MCP Server to be healthy before starting. Telegram Bot must wait for Backend to be healthy.
All services must communicate via isolated Docker network (annie-network). Only Backend API port should be exposed externally.
All services must pass health checks within 30 seconds of startup (p95). Health checks should have appropriate start periods to account for initialization.
Development volumes must mount service directories to enable hot-reload without rebuilding images. Volumes should not override container dependencies.
Dockerfiles should be named `Dockerfile` and placed in each service directory (backend/Dockerfile, mcp_server/Dockerfile, telegram_bot/Dockerfile).

interface.name: docker-compose.yml
interface.signature:
services: backend: build: ./backend ports: ["${BACKEND_PORT:-8000}:8000"] environment: [...] depends_on: redis: condition: service_healthy mcp-server: condition: service_healthy healthcheck: {...} volumes: ["./backend:/app"] networks: [annie-network]
mcp-server: build: ./mcp_server environment: [...] healthcheck: {...} volumes: ["./mcp_server:/app"] networks: [annie-network]
telegram-bot: build: ./telegram_bot environment: [...] depends_on: backend: condition: service_healthy healthcheck: {...} volumes: ["./telegram_bot:/app"] networks: [annie-network]
redis: image: redis:7.2-alpine ports: ["6379:6379"] healthcheck: {...} volumes: [redis-data:/data] networks: [annie-network]
networks: annie-network: driver: bridge
volumes: redis-data:

tests.standards: Manual verification required for this story. Test Docker Compose configuration syntax, service startup, health checks, and hot-reload functionality. Use docker-compose commands: `docker-compose config` (validate), `docker-compose up --build` (build and start), `docker-compose ps` (check health), `docker-compose logs` (view logs), `docker-compose down` (clean shutdown).

test.description: Verify docker-compose.yml defines all four services: backend, mcp-server, telegram-bot, redis
Verify each service has network configuration (annie-network) and proper dependencies (depends_on with condition: service_healthy)
Run `docker-compose up --build` and verify all services start without errors
Verify each service has healthcheck configuration with appropriate test, interval, timeout, retries, and start_period
Verify volume mounts are configured for hot-reload (./backend:/app, ./mcp_server:/app, ./telegram_bot:/app). Test by modifying a file and verifying changes reflect in container.
Start services and verify `docker-compose ps` shows all services as "healthy" within 30 seconds
